import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/credit_fraud.csv')

# Set the style for the plot
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axis
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create a boxplot for transaction amounts by transaction type and is_fraud status
sns.boxplot(
    x='transaction_type', 
    y='amount', 
    hue='is_fraud', 
    data=data, 
    palette='Set2'
)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Transaction Amounts by Type and Fraud Status')
plt.xlabel('Transaction Type')
plt.ylabel('Transaction Amount')
plt.legend(title='Is Fraud')

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/credit_fraud.csv')

# Set the style for the plot
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axis
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create a boxplot for transaction amounts by transaction type and is_fraud status
sns.boxplot(
    x='transaction_type', 
    y='amount', 
    hue='is_fraud', 
    data=data, 
    palette='Set2'
)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Transaction Amounts by Type and Fraud Status')
plt.xlabel('Transaction Type')
plt.ylabel('Transaction Amount')
plt.legend(title='Is Fraud')

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
